title: Add microbench for kernel-switch overhead + selector evaluation cost
author: Isabella Rossi
description:
Motivation: Kernel auto-selection v2 adds per-request decision telemetry (selected kernel, candidates, features). Before we increase sampling or add more fields, we need a hard bound on (a) kernel-switch overhead during mixed workloads, and (b) selector evaluation cost (feature extraction + candidate generation + scoring) on the hot path.

This PR adds a targeted microbenchmark suite to benchmark-lab that runs on representative SKUs (A100-80GB, H100-SXM, L40S) and measures: 1) steady-state decode with no switches (baseline), 2) forced alternating kernels every N steps (upper-bound switch cost), and 3) selector evaluation (v1 vs v2) with configurable feature vectors and candidate counts.

What’s included: - New bench: kernel_switch_overhead_bench (forces kernel alternation via a bench-only runtime hook) - New bench: selector_eval_cost_bench (pure CPU bench + optional end-to-end invocation) - Support for running against recorded request-shapes (prefill/decode tokens) to mimic real distributions - Standardized output JSON for perf-canary ingestion: p50/p95/p99 in ns/op and derived overhead ratios - Guardrails: fails the benchmark job if selector eval exceeds the configured budget on any SKU (defaults: p95 < 8us CPU-only, p95 < 25us end-to-end)

Results summary (collected on bench-lab runners; see artifacts): - Selector eval (v2) CPU-only: p95 3.7us (A100), 4.1us (H100), 5.4us (L40S) at 10 candidates; scales ~linear with candidates - End-to-end selector + registry lookup: p95 14–19us depending on SKU + registry size - Forced kernel alternation every step (worst-case): +1.2–2.8% throughput hit on decode-only loops; alternation every 16 steps is within noise on A100/H100, small but measurable on L40S

How this is used: - Provides the perf budget used by ENG-4824 to set telemetry sampling defaults and to justify adding candidate lists behind sampling - Provides a regression gate for future selector logic changes (ENG-4821/ENG-4825) - Serves as a reference for SRE when investigating tail spikes attributed to selector overhead

Notes/limitations: - This does NOT try to model full scheduler interactions or compilation cache misses; it’s intentionally scoped to isolate kernel-switch and selector evaluation overhead. - Kernel alternation uses a bench-only hook (compiled under BENCHMARK_LAB) to avoid exposing unstable knobs in production builds.

Checklist: - [x] Added benchmarks + docs - [x] Added CI job (runs on CPU always; GPU subset nightly + manual) - [x] Added artifact export for perf-canary - [x] Validated on A100 + H100 runners - [x] Linked to Linear tasks (ENG-4824/4825)

Follow-ups: - Add a mixed prefill+decode scenario with a long-context tail bucket (ties into ENG-4825). - Consider exporting an additional metric: selector_candidate_count distribution for correlation in perf-canary dashboards.

conversation: Claire Dubois: Can you clarify what exactly you mean by “kernel switch” here? Is this a host-side dispatch cost, a cache invalidation, or something else? We should be careful about conclusions.

Isabella Rossi (author): Good call. In this context it’s the incremental overhead observed when alternating between two already-compiled kernel variants in a tight decode loop, so it captures host dispatch + any device-side state changes that show up as throughput/latency deltas. It explicitly excludes compile/plan creation. I added a note in the README and renamed metrics to “forced alternation overhead” to avoid implying a single mechanism.

Omar El-Sayed: The selector eval numbers are the most important for telemetry. Can we emit both CPU-only and end-to-end (including registry lookup) and set budgets on p95? Also please add a way to scale candidates to 5/10/20/40.

Isabella Rossi (author): Done in 4b9c1c2. We now report selector_eval_cpu_ns and selector_eval_e2e_ns plus overhead ratio vs baseline. Candidates are parameterized; default run includes 5/10/20/40 and exports per-param stats. Budget defaults are p95 < 8us CPU-only and < 25us e2e; configurable via env vars in CI.
Sahana Iyer: CI concern: GPU runners are limited; can we keep presubmit CPU-only and move GPU to nightly + manual dispatch? Also ensure artifacts don’t explode in size.

Isabella Rossi (author): Updated workflow. Presubmit runs CPU-only (fast). GPU job is nightly + workflow_dispatch with SKU matrix. Artifact export is trimmed to percentiles + param metadata only (no raw samples).
Marcus Reed: Can we add a fixture-based request shape mode so we can approximate “real” distributions? It doesn’t need to be perfect; just keep it deterministic and small.

Isabella Rossi (author): Added request_shape_fixtures.json with a small set of (prefill_tokens, decode_tokens) pairs including mixed workloads; bench uses a fixed seed and iterates deterministically. Also added a “long_context_tail” fixture bucket for later expansion.
Marcus Reed: Looks good. Approving with one nit: make sure the bench-only hook is clearly compiled out for production builds.
Isabella Rossi (author): Added BENCHMARK_LAB guard + a comment in the hook header and README. Thanks.
Claire Dubois: Approved after the terminology tweak + README clarifications.
Omar El-Sayed: Approved. This gives us the perf budget we needed for ENG-4824.
